*[[2012 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2012 NCAA]] }} '''James Michael "Mike" Scott''' (born July 16, 1988) is an [[United States|American]] [[basketball]] player who recently completed his career at the [[University of Virginia]]. Scott, a 6'8" [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]] from [[Chesapeake, Virginia]], played his high school career at [[Deep Creek High School]] and then prepped for a year at [[Hargrave Military Academy]]. Scott signed with [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]] in 2007. After a solid first three years in which he led the team in [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounding]] as a sophomore and junior, Scott appeared poised for a breakout year in [[2010–11 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2010–11]]. He began the year averaging 15.9 [[Points per game|points]] and 10.2 rebounds in the team's first ten games. But Scott's season ended early as he suffered an ankle injury and underwent season-ending surgery.{{cite web|url=http://voices.washingtonpost.com/cavaliers-journal/2011/01/mike_scott_to_miss_remainder_o.html|title=Mike Scott to miss remainder of season due to ankle injury|accessdate=2012-03-27|date=2011-01-10|publisher=[[Washington Post]]}} Due to his injury, Scott was granted a [[Redshirt (college sports)|medical redshirt]] and a fifth year of eligibility. He was one of the top players in the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC) in [[2011–12 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|2011–12]], averaging 18.0 points and 8.3 rebounds per game and led the ACC in [[field goal percentage]] at .563. He led the Cavaliers to a 22-10 record and their first [[2012 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|NCAA tournament]] berth in five years, losing to [[2011–12 Florida Gators men's basketball team|Florida]] in the round of 64. Scott received conference recognition as the second-leading vote getter for the All-ACC team and national recognition as an [[2012 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] by the [[Sporting News]] (third team) and the [[Associated Press]] (Honorable Mention). Mike Scott finished his Virginia career with 1,538 points and is the third leading rebounder in Cavalier history with 944.{{cite web|url=http://www.virginiasports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=88842&SPID=10616&DB_OEM_ID=17800&ATCLID=1139456&Q_SEASON=2011|title=Mike Scott athletic biography|accessdate=2012-03-27|date=|publisher=University of Virginia athletics}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[http://www.virginiasports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=88842&SPID=10616&DB_OEM_ID=17800&ATCLID=1139456&Q_SEASON=2011 Virginia Athletic profile] {{Persondata | NAME = Mike, Scott | ALTERNATIVE NAMES = | SHORT DESCRIPTION = American college basketball player | DATE OF BIRTH = July 16, 1988 | PLACE OF BIRTH = | DATE OF DEATH = | PLACE OF DEATH = }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Scott, Mike}} [[Category:1988 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Basketball players from Virginia]] [[Category:People from Chesapeake, Virginia]] [[Category:Power forwards (basketball)]] [[Category:Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball players]]
